text: <highlight>XInclude</highlight> is an <highlight>XML feature</highlight> that allows one XML document to include content from another file using <highlight><xi:include></highlight> elements. It is processed at the <highlight>XML parsing stage</highlight> and does not require a <highlight>DOCTYPE</highlight> declaration like classic <highlight>XXE</highlight>.

The vulnerability occurs when the <highlight>XML parser</highlight> has <highlight>XInclude processing enabled</highlight> (e.g., <highlight>DOMDocument->xinclude()</highlight>) and <highlight>user-controlled XML input</highlight> is parsed without validation. The parser fetches <highlight>external resources</highlight> referenced in the <highlight>xi:include</highlight> element.

title: Difference from Classic XXE
items: Works even when <highlight>DTD processing</highlight> is disabled.
Looks like normal XML structure (less suspicious).

text: The dangerous part is <highlight>$dom->xinclude()</highlight>. This explicitly tells <highlight>libxml</highlight> to process <highlight><xi:include></highlight> elements and fetch <highlight>external resources</highlight>.
The parser fetches <highlight>/etc/passwd</highlight> and inserts its content into the XML output. <highlight>parse="text"</highlight> forces raw text inclusion instead of XML parsing.

title: How XInclude Works Internally
items: When <highlight>xinclude()</highlight> is called, <highlight>libxml</highlight> scans for <highlight><xi:include></highlight> nodes.
For each include node, libxml fetches the resource from <highlight>href</highlight>.
Content replaces the <highlight><xi:include></highlight> element in DOM tree.
Final DOM is serialized back to output.

text: If network access is allowed, the server makes a backend <highlight>HTTP request</highlight> to the internal service. This converts XInclude into an <highlight>SSRF primitive</highlight>.

Direct <highlight>RCE</highlight> is rare. XInclude is primarily a <highlight>file read primitive</highlight> or <highlight>SSRF vector</highlight>. However, if included content is later passed to <highlight>eval()</highlight>, <highlight>include()</highlight>, or template rendering engines, it may escalate to code execution.

If <highlight>DOCTYPE-based XXE</highlight> is blocked but XInclude works, you will see <highlight>external file content</highlight> reflected after adding <highlight>xmlns:xi</highlight> and <highlight>xi:include</highlight> elements.

code:
$dom->loadXML($xml, LIBXML_NONET | LIBXML_NOERROR | LIBXML_NOWARNING);
// DO NOT call $dom->xinclude();

text: Avoid calling <highlight>xinclude()</highlight>. Use <highlight>LIBXML_NONET</highlight> to block network access. Validate or sanitize XML input.

<highlight>XInclude</highlight> is an XML inclusion mechanism that can be abused for <highlight>file disclosure</highlight> and <highlight>SSRF</highlight> when <highlight>xinclude()</highlight> processing is enabled. It bypasses traditional <highlight>XXE defenses</highlight> because it does not rely on <highlight>DTD</highlight>.
